text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday.

- According to the findings of an international investigative commission on the Mostar incidents, law inforcement officers on both sides have been accused of unprofessional conduct. The Croat side has been fingered for shooting at a large group of Moslems visiting a cemetary in West Mostar.
- The Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) will win the elections in Zagreb with better results than before, says in an interview Zlatko Canjuga, head of the HDZ Zagreb city committee.
- Leading brewery Zagrebacka Pivovara, which is majority owned by Interbrew of Belgium, plans to boost production by three percent to over 1,000,000 hl of beer this year.
- A decision on whether the Varteks textile producer will retain its Levi's jeans licence will be made on April 15.
- Three days ahead of deadline, some 300,000 have still not filed their tax returns.
- Milan Vukovic appointed to preside over the Supreme Court replacing the suspended Krunislav Olujic.
- Mass privatisation programme to be launched soon after a list of government assets to be offered to beneficiaries is published. Media campaign planned to begin in April.
- Overheads fell to 62.5 percent of gross salaries this year from 69.9 in 1993, more tax relief announced.
- Stock market: Brokers welcome setting up of the securities depository.

- The coming Easter holiday will test the tourist potential of this summer's season. Istrian hoteliers see a 20 percent increase in the number of toursits from last year, others do not plan to open hotels.

- Splitska Banka's development strategy largely based on tourism, says Tomo Bolotin, its director during the overhaul and a likely president of the bank after rehabilitation. He says Splitska may seek a listing on Zagreb's bourse by year end.
- Several foreign companies, including Rurgas, interested in a project to develop natural gas infrastructure in coastal region of Dalmatia.
- Do the two incidents involving the blowing up of cars on the island of Korcula have to do with a drug traffickers vendetta? -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-4557075
